enterprise_rag.title: Enterprise-Ready RAG Agent
enterprise_rag.subtitle: An enterprise-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) AI agent that enables users to upload PDFs and ask natural-language questions.
enterprise_rag.overview: An enterprise-grade Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) AI agent that enables users to upload PDFs and ask natural-language questions. The system retrieves relevant document chunks via vector search (FAISS/ChromaDB) and generates grounded, citation-backed answers using LLMs (Llama 3.1/3.3 70B via Groq API), significantly reducing hallucinations compared to vanilla LLM chat. Includes an Arxiv Research Agent that detects research intent, searches arXiv, proposes papers, and auto-downloads them.
enterprise_rag.problem: Enterprise documents are difficult to search efficiently, and standalone LLMs cannot reliably answer questions without relevant contextual knowledge, causing hallucinated or unverified responses.
enterprise_rag.solution: Engineered a hybrid retrieval system pairing FAISS & ChromaDB vector embeddings with Google Gemini & Groq Llama 3.3 LLMs. Integrated recursive text chunking, metadata traceability, and page-level citation generation to ground answers strictly in source data.

architectureStages.name: Document Ingestion & Parsing
architectureStages.inputs: Raw PDF binary / multi-page documents (user upload or arXiv fetch)
architectureStages.outputs: Extracted text streams, restored Markdown tables, source metadata
architectureStages.responsibility: Extract document text with table-to-Markdown restoration and attach page numbers for traceability.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Chose PyMuPDF for fast C++ based extraction over PDFMiner; restored tables into Markdown syntax to preserve structured tabular relationships.

architectureStages.name: Recursive Semantic Chunking
architectureStages.inputs: Parsed Markdown text streams and document metadata
architectureStages.outputs: Overlapping semantic chunks (~200–500 tokens) with attached page metadata
architectureStages.responsibility: Split long documents into coherent semantic chunks while preserving paragraph boundaries and sentence continuity.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Implemented recursive character splitting with 10-15% chunk overlap instead of fixed-length token splitting to prevent truncating context mid-sentence.

architectureStages.name: Dual Vector Indexing
architectureStages.inputs: Semantic text chunks and source metadata dictionaries
architectureStages.outputs: Dense vector index (FAISS index file & ChromaDB collection)
architectureStages.responsibility: Generate vector embeddings and index high-dimensional vectors for ultra-low latency similarity queries.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Engineered a dual vector store strategy: in-memory FAISS index for high-speed sub-millisecond retrieval alongside ChromaDB for persistent document collections.

architectureStages.name: Similarity Retrieval & Context Injection
architectureStages.inputs: Natural-language query and conversation history
architectureStages.outputs: Top-K most relevant document chunks + injected structured prompt
architectureStages.responsibility: Query the vector index for top-K semantic chunks and direct queries via an intent router (document Q&A vs. arXiv research agent).
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Integrated an intent router to branch between local document Q&A and arXiv paper discovery; injected structured context prompts to constrain model knowledge.

architectureStages.name: LLM Inference & Generation
architectureStages.inputs: Injected context prompt + user question + conversation memory
architectureStages.outputs: Raw generated response strictly grounded in context chunks
architectureStages.responsibility: Synthesize natural language answers grounded strictly in retrieved chunks, eliminating hallucinated claims.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Designed a hot-swappable client abstraction supporting Llama 3.3 (70B) via Groq API for sub-5s latency, with fallback to Google Gemini.

architectureStages.name: Grounded Output & Citation Verification
architectureStages.inputs: Generated response and retrieved chunk source metadata
architectureStages.outputs: Formatted answer with expandable page-level citations and verified sources
architectureStages.responsibility: Validate synthesized facts against source chunks and render page-referenced citations in the Streamlit UI.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Enforced citation verification where every answer is paired with page and section references, reducing hallucinated responses by ~80%.

engineeringDecisions: Ingestion Pipeline: Used PyMuPDF-based PDF extraction with table-to-Markdown restoration and recursive semantic chunking to preserve paragraph meaning.
Vector Indexing: Embeddings stored in FAISS and ChromaDB for low-latency similarity search retrieving top-K relevant chunks.
Multi-Model Support: Hot-swappable between Llama 3.1, Llama 3.3 (70B), and Gemini via Groq API client layer.
Agentic Workflow: Intent detection router directs queries to document Q&A or automated arXiv paper discovery.
keyFeatures: PDF upload & real-time arXiv research paper integration
Advanced semantic text chunking with table-to-Markdown restoration
LLM-powered answers with page-level source citations
Multi-turn context-aware chat history & agent routing
enterprise_rag.challenges: Handling large PDF extractions with complex tabular figures and preventing context dilution when synthesizing answers across multi-page papers.
enterprise_rag.lessonsLearned: Chunk overlap strategy and metadata-aware retrieval matter far more for RAG accuracy than prompt engineering alone.

mlops.title: Vehicle Insurance MLOps Pipeline
mlops.subtitle: Production-grade automated ML training, versioning, containerization, and AWS cloud deployment pipeline.
mlops.overview: A production-grade, end-to-end MLOps pipeline for vehicle insurance risk prediction — from data ingestion through model deployment on AWS with fully automated CI/CD. Demonstrates the complete ML lifecycle: data management with MongoDB Atlas, model training/validation, containerized deployment via Docker, and automated continuous delivery using GitHub Actions to AWS EC2/ECR.
mlops.problem: Manual ML model training and deployment suffer from code drift, environment discrepancies, lack of reproducibility, and zero automated health monitoring.
mlops.solution: Designed a 6-stage modular pipeline using Python, Docker, GitHub Actions, and AWS ECR/EC2. Implemented automated data validation, model versioning, continuous integration, and seamless deployment triggers.
architecture: Docker Container Build & AWS ECR Push
GitHub Actions CI/CD to AWS EC2 Runner

architectureStages.outputs: Ingested training records with connection pooling

architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Integrated MongoDB Atlas for scalable cloud-hosted data storage and decoupled data persistence from training compute.

architectureStages.outputs: Validated dataset artifacts or automated pipeline abort signals
architectureStages.responsibility: Validate incoming dataset against predefined schema rules to prevent schema drift and bad inputs.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Implemented config-driven schema validation using config/schema.yaml to stop execution if column types or bounds drift.

architectureStages.name: Feature Transformation
architectureStages.inputs: Validated dataset
architectureStages.outputs: Transformed feature arrays and serialized preprocessor artifacts
architectureStages.responsibility: Apply feature scaling, categorical encoding, and transformation pipelines.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Serialized preprocessor object alongside model artifacts to guarantee exact feature consistency during inference.

architectureStages.name: Model Training & Evaluation
architectureStages.inputs: Transformed training features and production benchmark metrics
architectureStages.outputs: Trained model artifact and evaluation comparison score
architectureStages.responsibility: Train classification models and evaluate against S3-stored production benchmark thresholds.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Enforced automated model promotion: new models are pushed to production only if they outperform existing S3 benchmarks.

architectureStages.name: Docker Containerization
architectureStages.inputs: Application code, preprocessor, and model artifacts
architectureStages.outputs: Lightweight container image pushed to AWS Elastic Container Registry
architectureStages.responsibility: Package the prediction web service and model runtime into reproducible Docker containers.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Built optimized Dockerfile with .dockerignore to eliminate environmental discrepancies between dev, CI, and EC2 production.

architectureStages.name: Automated CI/CD Deployment
architectureStages.inputs: Git commit push to main branch
architectureStages.outputs: Live prediction microservice on AWS EC2 (port 5080)
architectureStages.responsibility: Automated build, test, ECR push, and zero-downtime deployment to EC2 self-hosted runner.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Set up GitHub Actions workflow authenticated via AWS IAM keys deploying to EC2 self-hosted runner, reducing deployment time by 85%.

engineeringDecisions: Data Layer: MongoDB Atlas integration with schema-driven validation using config/schema.yaml.
ML Pipeline: 6-stage sequential pipeline (Data Ingestion → Validation → Transformation → Training → Evaluation → Pusher).
Model Promotion: Automated evaluation against S3-stored production benchmarks; automated promotion only when new model exceeds threshold.
CI/CD Automation: GitHub Actions workflow authenticated with AWS IAM keys deploying to EC2 self-hosted runner.
keyFeatures: Automated S3 model benchmark evaluation & promotion
GitHub Actions automated CI/CD pipeline to AWS EC2
mlops.challenges: Debugging AWS ECR authentication credentials inside automated GitHub Actions workflows and resolving container port bindings on EC2.
mlops.lessonsLearned: Learned the critical importance of decoupling pipeline stages into modular components for zero-downtime container updates.

smart_feedback.title: Smart Feedback Collection & Analysis System
smart_feedback.subtitle: Scalable full-stack application featuring real-time feedback ingestion, MongoDB analytics, and automated reporting.
smart_feedback.overview: A full-stack web application that automates user feedback collection and sentiment analysis. The system ingests user-submitted feedback through a web interface, runs an NLP pipeline (tokenization → stop-word removal → polarity scoring) for automatic sentiment classification, and presents real-time analytics through admin dashboards with interactive charts.

smart_feedback.solution: Built a high-throughput Flask/Express REST API backend with NLTK sentiment preprocessing and an interactive Chart.js analytics dashboard.

NLP Pipeline: Built with NLTK for text preprocessing (tokenization, stop-word removal) and polarity scoring into positive/negative/neutral.
Security: Implemented JWT-based authentication with role-based authorization (admin vs. regular users).
Visualization: Interactive admin dashboard with Chart.js for real-time sentiment distribution visualization.
smart_feedback.challenges: Optimizing MongoDB / database aggregation queries to prevent bottlenecks under heavy concurrent submission loads.

crop_yield.title: Crop Yield Prediction Model
crop_yield.subtitle: Deep Learning agricultural yield prediction using Neural Networks, weather telemetry, and soil metrics.
crop_yield.overview: A deep neural network (DNN) model that predicts crop yield with 97% accuracy using agricultural and environmental input features. The model is trained on a Feed-Forward Neural Network architecture and considers soil nutrients (NPK levels), environmental factors (temperature, humidity, rainfall, pH), enabling farmers to make data-driven farming and resource-management decisions.
crop_yield.problem: Unpredictable climate conditions and unoptimized fertilizer usage cause significant crop yield variance for farmers.
crop_yield.solution: Engineered a TensorFlow/Keras deep neural network that analyzes 7 agricultural features (NPK levels, temperature, humidity, rainfall, pH) to forecast harvest yields.
engineeringDecisions: Model: Feed-Forward Neural Network built with TensorFlow/Keras handling multi-feature inputs (NPK, temperature, humidity, rainfall, pH).
Data Engineering: Feature engineering and preprocessing pipeline for diverse input types; handled missing values and normalization.
Deployment: Flask-based REST API for real-time inference and web interaction.
Scalability: Model architecture designed for extensibility supporting GPS-based field predictions.
keyFeatures: 7 input features (NPK, temp, humidity, rain, pH)
Flask REST API real-time inference endpoint

architectureStages.name: Categorical Encoding & Pipeline Assembly
architectureStages.inputs: Categorical features (airline, source city, destination city, stops)
architectureStages.outputs: Transformed, encoded feature matrix ready for regression modeling
architectureStages.responsibility: Encodes multi-class carrier and routing categories into sparse feature matrices.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Used Scikit-Learn Pipeline and ColumnTransformer to eliminate data leakage and ensure uniform pre-processing during inference.

architectureStages.name: Ensemble Model Training & Hyperparameter Tuning
architectureStages.inputs: Preprocessed training feature matrices and ticket price labels
architectureStages.outputs: Tuned ensemble model achieving 96.95% R2 score on test data
architectureStages.responsibility: Trains ensemble regressor capturing non-linear interactions between routes, carrier, and timing.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Tuned Random Forest with RandomizedSearchCV for optimal tree depth and estimators, achieving high predictive accuracy across diverse routes.

architectureStages.name: Model Artifact Serialization
architectureStages.inputs: Trained Random Forest regressor and fitted preprocessors
architectureStages.outputs: Serialized pipeline artifacts ready for deployment
architectureStages.responsibility: Persists trained model and transformers for instant, zero-recalculation loading.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Serialized full preprocessing pipeline alongside the estimator to guarantee zero feature discrepancy during live API calls.

architectureStages.name: Real-Time Price Prediction Web Service
architectureStages.inputs: User flight search inputs (airline, route, departure date, stops)
architectureStages.outputs: Instant estimated ticket fare and expected cost savings indicator
architectureStages.responsibility: Serves live fare estimations via clean web interface, enabling ~20% average cost savings.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Deployed Flask backend with responsive client interface providing instant fare estimates upon form completion.

polyglot.title: Polyglot AI – Language Detection System
polyglot.subtitle: High-precision Natural Language Processing classification model detecting 20+ world languages.
polyglot.overview: A multilingual language detection system using Linear SVM (Scikit-learn) that automatically identifies the language of input text across 17+ languages with 99%+ accuracy. Deployed as a REST API for integration into multilingual content processing pipelines.
polyglot.problem: Global software applications require instant language identification for automated content routing and localization.
polyglot.solution: Trained a Linear SVM classifier with character n-gram TF-IDF features capable of sub-millisecond language detection across 17+ international languages.
engineeringDecisions: Model: Linear SVM classifier with TF-IDF feature extraction trained on multilingual text corpus spanning 17+ languages.
API: REST API endpoint for real-time language detection designed for pipeline integration.
Preprocessing: Text normalization and feature engineering optimized for cross-lingual character patterns.
keyFeatures: Linear SVM & TF-IDF n-gram feature extraction
polyglot.challenges: Distinguishing between closely related Romance and Slavic languages on very short sentence fragments.
polyglot.lessonsLearned: Character n-grams are vastly superior to word tokens when identifying languages with flexible syntax.

architectureStages.name: Multilingual Corpus Ingestion
architectureStages.inputs: Raw text samples across 17+ languages (Latin, Cyrillic, Asian, Indic scripts)
architectureStages.outputs: Consolidated, labeled multilingual training dataset
architectureStages.responsibility: Ingests diverse text corpora representing distinct language families.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Balanced multilingual datasets across 17+ languages to prevent dominant language bias in classifier decision boundaries.

architectureStages.name: Text Normalization & Cleansing
architectureStages.inputs: Raw multilingual text strings containing punctuation, URLs, and numbers
architectureStages.outputs: Standardized text strings preserving script-specific character sets
architectureStages.responsibility: Removes extraneous symbols and digits while strictly preserving language-specific alphabets.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Preserved unique unicode ranges and diacritical marks essential for accurate low-resource language discrimination.

architectureStages.name: Character N-Gram & TF-IDF Extraction
architectureStages.inputs: Cleaned multilingual text samples
architectureStages.outputs: High-dimensional character n-gram TF-IDF sparse matrix
architectureStages.responsibility: Extracts sub-word character n-gram patterns that generalize across grammar and vocabulary.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Selected sub-word character n-grams (3-5 characters) over word tokens, allowing accurate language detection even for short fragments.

architectureStages.name: Linear SVM Classifier Optimization
architectureStages.inputs: TF-IDF feature matrices and language class labels
architectureStages.outputs: Optimized Linear Support Vector Classifier with 99%+ accuracy
architectureStages.responsibility: Trains maximum-margin hyperplanes to separate 17+ language classes in high-dimensional space.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Chose Linear Support Vector Classification for sub-millisecond inference speed and exceptional performance on high-dimensional text data.

architectureStages.name: Cross-Lingual Evaluation & Benchmark
architectureStages.inputs: Held-out multilingual test set
architectureStages.outputs: Confusion matrix and precision/recall metrics (>99% across all 17 classes)
architectureStages.responsibility: Evaluates classification accuracy and validates zero degradation across similar languages.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Validated model performance on challenging closely-related language pairs (e.g., Spanish vs. Portuguese; Hindi vs. Marathi).

architectureStages.name: REST API Gateway Deployment
architectureStages.inputs: JSON payload containing arbitrary text snippet
architectureStages.outputs: Predicted language ISO code and classification confidence score
architectureStages.responsibility: Provides real-time language detection microservice for integration into larger NLP pipelines.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Built lightweight REST endpoint with sub-10ms response time designed for plug-and-play integration into automated translation pipelines.

cloudcast.title: Cloudcast Weather App
cloudcast.subtitle: Polished web application delivering real-time weather telemetry with a sleek dynamic UI.
cloudcast.overview: A responsive weather application built with vanilla JavaScript and CSS that fetches real-time weather data from live APIs, dynamically updates the UI based on weather conditions, and presents current and forecasted weather information with an intuitive, visually engaging interface.
cloudcast.problem: Standard weather dashboards are cluttered with ad banners and lack responsive, intuitive user interfaces.
cloudcast.solution: Built a clean vanilla JavaScript app with dynamic background weather transitions and OpenWeather REST API integration, deployed on GitHub Pages.
engineeringDecisions: Frontend: Pure JavaScript with CSS for responsive design and dynamic UI theming based on current weather conditions.
API Integration: Third-party Weather API consumption with error handling and rate limiting.
Deployment: Static site deployed on GitHub Pages for zero-cost hosting.
cloudcast.challenges: Handling API rate limit edge cases and smooth UI state transitions during network latency.
cloudcast.lessonsLearned: Vanilla JavaScript and native CSS variables can deliver unmatched speed and aesthetic elegance.

architectureStages.name: User Location & Search Input Capture
architectureStages.inputs: User city search query or browser Geolocation API coordinates
architectureStages.outputs: Sanitized location string or latitude/longitude coordinates
architectureStages.responsibility: Captures user search queries with client-side sanitization and validation.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Supported dual location input: direct city text search and native browser geolocation for instant local weather discovery.

architectureStages.name: Asynchronous Weather API Dispatch
architectureStages.inputs: Location query parameters
architectureStages.outputs: Raw JSON response containing current weather, atmospheric data, and 5-day forecast
architectureStages.responsibility: Dispatches secure asynchronous HTTP requests to OpenWeather REST APIs.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Implemented robust error handling, network retry, and client-side response caching to prevent duplicate API hits.

architectureStages.name: Telemetry Parsing & Metric Extraction
architectureStages.inputs: Raw OpenWeather JSON payload
architectureStages.outputs: Structured telemetry state (temperature, humidity, wind, pressure, UV index, forecast array)
architectureStages.responsibility: Transforms deeply nested API response into normalized application state objects.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Designed pure JavaScript data transformation utilities without external dependencies, keeping application bundle under 50KB.

architectureStages.name: Dynamic Glassmorphic Theme Engine
architectureStages.inputs: Current weather condition code (Clear, Rain, Clouds, Snow, Thunderstorm)
architectureStages.outputs: Dynamically adjusted CSS background gradients, accent colors, and atmospheric overlays
architectureStages.responsibility: Adapts visual atmosphere and color palette in real time based on local weather conditions.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Used CSS variables and glassmorphic backdrop filters for fluid theme transitions without layout reflows.

architectureStages.name: Responsive Forecast DOM Rendering
architectureStages.inputs: Normalized current weather and 5-day forecast state
architectureStages.outputs: Rendered weather metric cards, interactive temperature gauges, and forecast cards
architectureStages.responsibility: Updates DOM nodes with smooth animations and responsive mobile-first layouts.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Employed modular DOM update functions to update only modified weather metric nodes rather than re-rendering the whole page.

architectureStages.name: Static Edge Deployment & Caching
architectureStages.inputs: Static HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript asset bundle
architectureStages.outputs: Globally accessible, CDN-cached weather intelligence web application
architectureStages.responsibility: Delivers zero-maintenance, high-availability web application to end users.
architectureStages.engineeringDecision: Architected as a pure client-side progressive static site deployed on GitHub Pages for zero hosting cost and near-instant initial paint.
